summary.title: Compile by Training: Turning Natural-Language Specifications into Local Neural Functions

setting_and_object.category: System (compiler/service artifact) built on an algorithmic pipeline

details: Many recurring text-to-text functions are easy to describe in natural language but too fuzzy for hand-written rules, while calling a large remote LLM per input incurs repeated cost, latency, and provider dependence.
Program-as-Weights' amortized (one forward pass) compiler is fast but spends fixed computation per function, leaving accuracy on the table for hard specifications.

'Compile by training': a compiler that turns a natural-language specification into a reusable local neural function by (1) having teacher LLMs synthesize a task-specific input-output dataset from the spec and (2) gradient-training a LoRA adapter plus prompt scaffold that specializes a small shared frozen interpreter, warm-started from the amortized PAW weight predictor.
The output is a packaged .paw program artifact that runs locally without teacher calls and can be stored, versioned, cached, and composed like ordinary software.
Deployed as an interactive minute-scale build service in which teacher synthesis, model loading, and training are overlapped (streaming compile) and compiles run as persistent background jobs.
Interpreter: frozen quantized Qwen3-0.6B shared across all programs.
Teachers: GPT-5.4-mini and GPT-5.5 in a 2:1 mixture, prompted for strict-JSON example pairs, with validation rejecting malformed batches.
Data: 2400 unique synthesized pairs expanded to 6400 training examples.
Optimization: LoRA rank 64, alpha 16, hypernetwork (amortized PAW) initialization; batch 48, 100 steps, cosine LR decay (lr 2e-4 in sweeps).
Metric: LLM Exact Match (LEM), a GPT-5.5 judge deciding semantic correctness given spec, input, reference, and prediction, tolerating cosmetic/format differences.
Judge validation: 0.977 accuracy, Cohen's kappa 0.946 against 128 author labels (GPT-5.4-mini judge: 0.938 / 0.858).
Benchmark: FuzzyBench-Hard, the subset of FuzzyBench specs on which the PAW fast amortized compiler produced zero exact matches.
Baseline: PAW's fast one-forward-pass amortized compiler.
Teacher mixture: 3600 mini-only pairs vs 2400 mini + 1200 GPT-5.5, holding batch 64, lr 2e-4, 100 steps fixed.
Data scaling: 1440 / 2400 / 3600 / 7200 unique pairs at batch 48.
Cold compile (no cached teacher outputs) of a representative spec timed on B300, H200, and an RTX GPU.
Load test with four concurrent compile jobs across shared GPU workers with a job queue, teacher-output cache, and shared artifact store.
paw-helper: 30 compiled programs (28 in live routing) in one backend serving four websites, mixing compiled fuzzy classifiers/answerers/validators with deterministic BM25 retrieval and control flow.
Avatar Director: a compiled program mapping natural-language commands to a browser-validated action DSL, checked on 44 hand-authored validation instructions.
Claudish translator: one compiled adapter per direction (English-to-Claudish and back) on the shared 0.6B interpreter, publicly deployed.

key_findings.finding: Investing about a minute of compile-time training instead of a single forward pass yields a large correctness gain on specifications the fast compiler fails.
key_findings.evidence: On FuzzyBench-Hard mean LEM rises from 0.224 (PAW fast amortized compiler) to 0.836, a 0.612 absolute improvement, at a compile cost of 50.9 s versus 3.5 s.

key_findings.finding: Mixing a stronger teacher with a cheap teacher improves compiled-function quality more than scaling synthetic data volume alone.
key_findings.evidence: On development specs with 3600 unique pairs, a 2:1 GPT-5.4-mini/GPT-5.5 mixture reaches 0.851 LEM vs 0.746 for mini-only; separately, scaling unique pairs from 1440 to 7200 only moves LEM from 0.821 to 0.866 (0.836 at both 2400 and 3600).

key_findings.finding: Minute-scale training compilation can be made interactive by overlapping teacher synthesis with training and treating compiles as queued background jobs.
key_findings.evidence: Cold compiles took 50.9 s (B300), 68.2 s (H200), and 99.2 s (RTX); a four-job concurrent load test completed all jobs with 1.01 s mean queue wait and even worker utilization, with teacher synthesis identified as the dominant latency term that the streaming path hides.

key_findings.finding: Independently compiled neural functions compose with ordinary code into deployed multi-component applications.
key_findings.evidence: paw-helper runs 30 compiled programs (28 live-routed) over four websites, combining compiled classification/answering/selection with BM25 Piazza retrieval; the Claudish translator served 100,747 successful requests between Aug 22 and Sep 2, 2026.

key_findings.finding: Compiled 0.6B functions can emit structured executable programs, not just labels or free text.
key_findings.evidence: Avatar Director's compiled program produced the expected action-DSL structure on 43 of 44 hand-authored validation instructions, with browser-side validation and rendering.
